script.title: Company vs Partnership Firm
script.caption_hook: Same business, different person: company vs partnership firm

lines.say: Same business, but a company and a firm are different? How?
A company is a separate person in law. A firm is just the partners together.
Separate person? Like it can own things?
Yes. A company owns property, and can sue or be sued in its own name. A firm acts through its partners.
And if the business has debts? Who pays?
Shareholders of a limited company are liable only up to the unpaid amount on their shares. Partners have unlimited liability.
Oh! And what if a partner dies?
A firm is dissolved on a partner's death unless the partners have agreed otherwise. A company has perpetual succession.
So registration must be compulsory for both, right?
Compulsory for a company. Optional for a firm. Laws differ too: Companies Act, 2013, and Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
So does a firm have any veil?
Exactly, a firm has no veil, so partners stand exposed. A company has one, though courts can lift it in fraud cases.
Remember: a company is a separate person. A firm is its partners together.

Checker: Line 12 (voice): 'Exactly' doesn't answer Line 11, which asks a question rather than stating something. Better: 'No, a firm has no separate veil, so partners stand exposed. A company has one, though courts can lift it in cases such as fraud or improper conduct.' Fraud is only one ground for lifting the veil, so 'in fraud cases' reads as if it were the only one.

Checker: Line 4 (voice): 'A firm acts through its partners' can suggest that a firm can never sue or be sued in its own name. Under Order XXX of the CPC, partners may sue or be sued in the firm name for convenience. The firm still isn't a separate legal person. Better: 'A firm is not a separate legal person; its property and liabilities are the partners' own, though for convenience it may sue or be sued in the firm name.'
Checker: Line 6 (board, left panel): 'Limited / if Ltd company' repeats the 'Ltd Co.' title and adds nothing. Better: 'Limited / to unpaid share amount'.
